2027-02-27.title: Third Saturday of the Great Fast
2027-02-27.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: The evils to be put away
The kingdom of God belongs to those who repent
2027-02-27.alt: Season of the Great Fast (Sauma Ramba).
2027-02-27.verse: and be kind to one another, tenderhearted, forgiving one another, as God in Christ has forgiven you.
theo: Paul writes about the most ordinary place of holiness: the way we talk to one another. “So then, putting away falsehood, let all of us speak the truth to our neighbors, for we are members of one another.” A lie told to a brother is like one hand deceiving the other. Then a realistic word about anger: “Be angry but do not sin; do not let the sun go down on your anger, and do not make room for the devil.” Anger is not always sin, but anger kept overnight becomes a room rented to the devil. The thief is not only to stop stealing but to work honestly “so as to have something to share with the needy.” And speech is to build up: “Let no evil talk come out of your mouths, but only what is useful for building up, as there is need, so that your words may give grace to those who hear.” Paul reminds the baptised that they carry a seal: “do not grieve the Holy Spirit of God, with which you were marked with a seal for the day of redemption.” The Holy Spirit is grieved by bitterness at the dinner table as much as by great crimes. Many Syro-Malabar families keep a beautiful custom that answers this word: after the night prayer the children greet their parents and elders, “Praise be to Jesus Christ”, and receive the answer, “Now and for ever, Amen.” It is hard to go to sleep angry after saying that. Paul ends with the verse that could be written over every Christian home: “Put away from you all bitterness and wrath and anger and wrangling and slander, together with all malice, and be kind to one another, tenderhearted, forgiving one another, as God in Christ has forgiven you.”

In the Gospel Jesus tells a short parable in the temple. A father asks his two sons to work in the vineyard. One says, “I will not”; but later he changed his mind and went. The other answers politely, “I go, sir”; but he did not go. “Which of the two did the will of his father?” The answer is obvious, and it is aimed at people who had always said yes to God with their lips. “Truly I tell you, the tax collectors and the prostitutes are going into the kingdom of God ahead of you.” They had said no to God for years, but when John came preaching repentance, they changed their minds and believed. The religious leaders saw it happen, “and even after you saw it, you did not change your minds and believe him.” The parable has two warnings and one hope. Saying yes is not the same as going; and a past no is not the last word. The Great Fast is the time of “later he changed his mind.” On Saturday evenings in these weeks, the queues for confession grow longer in many parishes. Every person standing in that line is the son who once said no, and is now going into the vineyard.
outline: Ask: where have I said yes to God and not gone?
Truth, anger and the setting sun.
Do not grieve the Holy Spirit.
Yes without going, and no that turns into yes.
“be kind to one another, tenderhearted, forgiving one another, as God in Christ has forgiven you.”
live: Settle one quarrel before you sleep tonight, even if it is only with a word.
Do today the one thing you promised God and have not yet done; if it is confession, go this evening.
2027-02-27.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, you sealed us with your Holy Spirit for the day of redemption. Keep us from grieving him with bitterness, anger and slander; let our words give grace to those who hear them, and let the sun never set on our anger. Where we have said yes to you and not gone, and where we have said no, change our minds and send us into your vineyard. Amen.
altar: At the Holy Qurbana we are made members of one body; before we receive Christ we forgive one another, as God in Christ has forgiven us.

quick: Paul: do not let the sun go down on your anger.
Let your words give grace to those who hear.
The son who said no but went did the will of his father.
2027-02-27.action: Settle one quarrel before you sleep tonight.
2027-02-27.question: Where have I said yes to God and not gone?

family.explain: A father asked his two sons to help in the vineyard. One said no, but later he felt sorry and went to work. The other said yes, but never went! Jesus asks: which son really obeyed? It is not enough to say yes to God; we must also do it. And if we have said no, we can always change our minds.
family.intention: We pray for anyone in our family who is angry or hurt tonight.
family.ask: Ask: “Before we go to sleep, is there anyone we need to make peace with?”

illus: When a rubber farmer near Kanjirappally fell ill, he asked his son, home from college, to do the morning tapping. The boy said: I cannot, Appa, I have exams, and I am not getting up at four. His father said nothing. The next morning the mother woke before dawn and saw a small headlamp moving among the rubber trees. At breakfast no one mentioned it. But that evening, after the night prayer, when the son came for the blessing, the father held his hand a little longer than usual.

pm.open: Lord, you sealed us with your Spirit. Guard our tongues and soften our hearts as we pray. Amen.
share: Do not let the sun go down on your anger (Ephesians 4:26). What anger have I carried for more than a day?
So that your words may give grace (Ephesians 4:29). Whose day have I made heavier by my words?
Later he changed his mind and went (Matthew 21:29). What no can I turn into a yes this week?
pm.resp: Lord, make us kind and tenderhearted.
interc: For the Church, that her words may always give grace.
For families where anger is carried from day to day.
For those preparing for confession this evening.
For those who have said no to God for many years.
For our group, that we may forgive as God in Christ has forgiven us.
pm.close: Father, you are patient with sons who say no and with sons who say yes and do not go. Change our minds, send us into your vineyard, and make us kind to one another. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, Paul speaks to us about our everyday words. Speak the truth to your neighbours, for we are members of one another. Be angry but do not sin; do not let the sun go down on your anger (Ephesians 4:25–26).

Let no evil talk come out of your mouths, he says, but only words that build up and give grace to those who hear (Ephesians 4:29). Bitterness at the table grieves the Holy Spirit with whom we were sealed.
Jesus tells us of two sons. One says I will not, but later changes his mind and goes. The other says I go, sir, but does not go (Matthew 21:28–30). Which one did the will of his father?

Saying yes is not the same as going, and a past no is not the last word. The Great Fast is the time to change our minds. Let us make peace before the sun goes down, and go into the Father's vineyard today. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus told a story about two sons. One said no but then went to help his father. The other said yes but never went! Let us not only say yes to God, let us do it.

intro: Theme: “be kind to one another, tenderhearted, forgiving one another, as God in Christ has forgiven you.”
Truth and anger among members of one body, words that give grace, and the son who changed his mind.

sub: Do not make room for the devil.
q: A soft answer turns away wrath, but a harsh word stirs up anger.
Be angry but do not sin; do not let the sun go down on your anger,
points.apply: End no day this week without settling the day's quarrels.

q: Set a guard over my mouth, O LORD; keep watch over the door of my lips.
Let no evil talk come out of your mouths, but only what is useful for building up, as there is need, so that your words may give grace to those who hear.
points.apply: Say one word of encouragement to each member of your family today.

points.h: He changed his mind and went
sub: I go, sir, and did not go.
q: Again, when the wicked turn away from the wickedness they have committed and do what is lawful and right, they shall save their life.

For John came to you in the way of righteousness and you did not believe him, but the tax collectors and the prostitutes believed him; and even after you saw it, you did not change your minds and believe him.
points.apply: Do today what you promised God and have not yet done.

concl: We are members of one another: let the sun never set on our anger, and let our words give grace.
A yes without going is empty; a no can still become a yes. Now is the time to go into the vineyard.
2027-02-27.resolve: Make your Lenten confession, if you have not yet made it, before the Fourth Sunday of the Great Fast.
